answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity, whether named copper, zenith, or raven, to lock a refundable bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs, with only one active bid per bond. Creating more identities does not create free bidding capacity: an attacker running 1,000 identities must immobilize 1,000 bonds. The delay prevents rapid reuse of the same funds, making a sybil swarm costly in capital and foregone returns.
